newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-BOWE QUITS MARINES AFTER THREE DAYS OF BOOT CAMP.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-BOWE QUITS MARINES AFTER THREE DAYS OF BOOT CAMP.

text.p: Former heavyweight champion Riddick Bowe, who with big fanfare last month said he was realising a life-long dream by joining the Marines, quit after just three days of Boot Camp because he missed his children, his manager said Friday.
Bowe's manager, Rock Newman, told CNN in an interview that Bowe had gone through agony being away from his wife and children.
"Once he got there it was more than he expected," Newman added.

The Marines said in a prepared statement that Bowe, "has stated that his reason for not continuing training was that at this stage of his life he was having difficulty adapting to an extremely regimented lifestyle.
"He said he wished he would have enlisted in the Marine Corps earlier in his life."

"After considerable and thoughtful discussion between his senior drill instructor and his battalion commander on whether he would continue the 12-week training programme, the Marine Corps has released Bowe," it said.
Bowe, 29, was accepted into the rigours of the Marine Corps Reserves after extensive interviews with Marine officers and received waivers for age, weight and dependants.

The Corps said it had cautioned Bowe "regarding the rigours of recruit training" before his arrival at Parris Island (South Carolina) and had encouraged and allowed him to visit the training site before he began.
Bowe, at a packed Manhattan news conference last month, proudly announced he was joing the Marines.
Wearing a Marine Corps cap inscribed with "The Few, The Proud" and practicing his salute, Bowe said he was looking forward to serving his country.
"If war breaks out I'm going to war," he said. "If I gotta die defending my country, what a way to die."
The Marines said Bowe, who entered the Marines on February 10 but did not begin Boot Camp until this week, should be processed out of the Corps on Friday afternoon.
The regimented Marine lifestyle includes getting up at 0500, extensive physical training, hand-to-hand combat practice, and lights out by 9 p.m.
Many boxing observers had thought Marine Corps training would at least get him in top physical shape, which he has had trouble doing in the past.
As a Marine Reservist, Bowe would have owed the Marines three years of active duty one weekend a month after Boot Camp.
Bowe (40-1) won the heavyweight title by beating Evander Holyfield in November, 1992, and lost it to Holyfield a year later.
Bowe's last two fights were disasters.
He won both of them against Andrew Golota, but only when Golota was disqualified each time for low blows after thoroughly beating Bowe, often battering him around the ring like a rag doll.
There was no immediate word on Bowe's boxing future.
